title: Light left after many uncoated surfaces
caption: Each uncoated air–glass surface transmits 96%, so N surfaces transmit 0.96^N. For the lens with 10 surfaces that is 0.96¹⁰ = 0.66: about 34% of the light is lost, much of it as stray reflections that cause flare, which is why lenses are coated.
alt: Graph of transmitted fraction against the number of air–glass surfaces from 0 to 12: a decaying curve passing 0.66 at 10 surfaces.
description: The horizontal axis is the number of uncoated air–glass surfaces N; the vertical axis is the fraction of light transmitted.
Each surface transmits 96%, so the fraction is 0.96^N, drawn as a smooth curve.
At N = 10 it is 0.96¹⁰ = 0.66, so 34% is lost.
